title: The Dallewalia misl
hookLine: a misl north of the Sutlej

cards: On a map of the Punjab, the rivers run down from the mountains like fingers spread across the plain. Between them lie the doabs, the land between two rivers.
The riders lived with those rivers: where to cross, when the water was high, which bank you held. Today's band held country along the Sutlej, on its north side.
Its name came from a village, but its life came from the water. Today: the Dallewalia misl.

teach.b: Three pieces. The name: tradition says the band began with a Sikh from a village called Dallewal, and the riders who joined him were called after it, the Dallewalias. You know the pattern now: a village, a chief, a band.
The chief people remembered: tradition says it was Tara Singh, called Ghaiba, a hard-riding chief who built up its lands along the Sutlej.
In the way Sikh histories tell it, he held his own among bigger misls, and the band's strength rose and fell with him. Then the river.
For a misl north of the Sutlej, the river was a road, a border and a lifeline at once. It watered the fields that fed the riders. It slowed an army coming from the other bank.

It marked where one band's country ended and another's began. Holding land by a river meant knowing it well: the fords, the flood season, the banks that shift. Rivers in this country carry Sikh memory too.
North of the Sutlej, at Sultanpur, runs the little river Bein.

teach.h: THE BEIN, WHERE GURU NANAK WENT IN.
teach.b: Tradition says Guru Nanak went into its water one morning and did not come out for days, and came back with the words: there is no Hindu, there is no Muslim.
Long before any misl rode, tradition sets a turning point of the Sikh story at a river in the same country. The Dallewalias lived by the river.

how: Sikhs meet the Dallewalia misl in Sikh histories, and remember the river Bein at Sultanpur Lodhi, where Gurdwara Ber Sahib marks Guru Nanak's time in its water.

games.q: you hold land on the north bank of the Sutlej. an army is coming from the south. what does the river do for you?
o: nothing; rivers don't matter in war.
it slows the army, if you know the fords.
it carries your riders downstream to the sea.
games.why: a river band lived by knowing the fords and the flood season; the river slowed an army from the other bank.

practice: Bring to mind the nearest river to where you live, or one you've known: its color, its sound, the bridge you cross it on, and if you don't know its name, just notice that.
Picture where it comes from and where it goes, and let it keep flowing in your mind on each breath out, with Waheguru if you pray.

wordCard.voice: Dallewal, the village that gave the Dallewalia misl its name, built up by Tara Singh Ghaiba, holding land along the north side of the Sutlej. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi for Sutlej, the river along which the Dallewalias held land.

carryVoice: Your line: by the river. Road, border and lifeline, all at once. Eight hundred ninety-four days, and counting.
